title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 167 (Vacation of office of director)

content.overview: Section 167 provides that the office of a director shall become vacant in case the director incurs any of the disqualifications specified in section 164; absents himself from all the meetings of the Board of Directors held during a period of twelve months with or without seeking leave of absence; acts in contravention of section 184 relating to entering into contracts or arrangements in which he is directly or indirectly interested; fails to disclose his interest in any contract or arrangement in which he is directly or indirectly interested in contravention of section 184; becomes disqualified by an order of a court or the Tribunal; is convicted of an offence involving moral turpitude or otherwise and sentenced to imprisonment for not less than six months; or is removed in pursuance of the provisions of the Act. A private company may provide additional grounds in its articles.
content.glance: Office vacates automatically on s. 164 disqualification, 12-month absence from all board meetings, s. 184 contraventions, court/Tribunal disqualification, conviction with ≥6 months’ imprisonment, or removal; private companies may add article grounds.
content.study: The office of a director shall become vacant if he incurs any of the disqualifications specified in section 164; absents himself from all the meetings of the Board held during a period of twelve months with or without seeking leave of absence of the Board; acts in contravention of the provisions of section 184 relating to entering into contracts or arrangements in which he is directly or indirectly interested; fails to disclose his interest in contravention of section 184; becomes disqualified by an order of a court or the Tribunal; is convicted of an offence involving moral turpitude or otherwise and sentenced in respect thereof to imprisonment for not less than six months; or is removed in pursuance of the provisions of this Act. Where a director incurs disqualification under section 164(2), the office of the director shall become vacant in all the companies other than the company which is in default under that subsection. A private company may, by its articles, provide any other ground for vacation. If a person continues to act as director after the office has become vacant, he is liable to the penalty provided. Current-law framing: identify the ground; apply automatic vacation; note s. 164(2) multi-company effect; distinguish resignation (s. 168) and removal (s. 169).

sections.heading: Disqualification Ground
sections.body: Office vacates if the director incurs any disqualification under section 164. Under s. 164(2), vacation applies in all companies other than the defaulting company.

sections.heading: Absence
sections.body: Absence from all Board meetings held during a period of twelve months, with or without leave, vacates the office.

sections.heading: Interest / Disclosure
sections.body: Acting in contravention of section 184, or failing to disclose interest under section 184, vacates the office.

sections.heading: Court / Conviction / Removal
sections.body: Court or Tribunal disqualification order; conviction with imprisonment of not less than six months; or removal under the Act — each vacates the office.

sections.heading: Private-Company Articles
sections.body: A private company may provide additional grounds for vacation in its articles.

examples.title: Twelve-month absence
examples.body: A director attends no Board meeting for twelve consecutive months. Under s. 167 the office becomes vacant whether or not leave was sought.

examples.title: s. 164(2) multi-company effect
examples.body: A person is a director of Company A (in default under s. 164(2)) and Company B. The office becomes vacant in Company B (and other non-defaulting companies), not in Company A under the s. 164(2) rule as framed.

hypotheticals.question: Is a board resolution required to vacate the office when a s. 167 ground occurs?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Vacation under section 167 is automatic on the occurrence of a stated ground. A resolution may record the fact but is not the source of the vacancy.

distinctions.title: Vacation (s. 167) vs resignation (s. 168) vs removal (s. 169)
distinctions.right: Resignation is voluntary notice; removal is by ordinary resolution after special notice

misconceptions.trap: Absence from some but not all meetings in twelve months vacates the office.
misconceptions.correction: Section 167 requires absence from all Board meetings held during a period of twelve months.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 167 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify the ground. II. Apply automatic vacation. III. Note s. 164(2) multi-company effect if relevant. IV. Distinguish resignation/removal. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Ground facts; automatic vacation; multi-company effect if any; precise relief.

enhancement.definition: Section 167 provides that a director’s office becomes vacant automatically on the statutory grounds listed, including s. 164 disqualification, twelve-month absence from all Board meetings, and s. 184 contraventions.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Certain events are incompatible with continued occupancy of the office of director and operate without a separate removal resolution.

enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 167 is the automatic-vacation provision complementary to disqualification, resignation and removal.
